_comment: Provenance for schemas vendored from tinyland-inc/site.scaffold, which the
$id of both manifest schemas already names as the authority. Recording the
source revision and per-file digests is what makes the vendoring auditable:
before this file, ci-templates carried a COPY of the v1 schema with no lock
and no drift gate, and it had silently diverged from its source in BOTH
gained a gitops_receiver prohibition). Nothing compared them.
The v2 copy arrived the same way and is currently byte-identical to its
source. This file exists so that stays a checkable fact rather than a
coincidence -- it is the cheapest moment a drift gate will ever be added.
v1 is recorded as DRIFTED on purpose. This change does not silently adopt
upstream's v1 bytes -- that would change what every consumer is validated
against, which is a separate decision with its own review. It records the
divergence so the drift gate can report it instead of nobody noticing.
Re-vendoring recipe: copy the source file, recompute sha256 for both the
vendored copy and (for a drifted entry) the upstream one, and update
source_revision in the same change. `just vendored-schema-provenance-check`
verifies the vendored digests offline; it deliberately does NOT reach
site.scaffold, so upstream freshness stays a separate, non-blocking question.
source_revision_note: site.scaffold main @ 2026-08-29. Both schema files are byte-identical at 6c58bb630de1 and at this revision, so recording the newer tip is a provenance refresh, not a content change.

files.state_note: Known divergence, reported not reconciled. ci-templates alone defines authorities.artifact_registry; site.scaffold alone forbids authorities.gitops_receiver on a static spoke. De-forking v1 changes what live consumers are validated against and is its own change.
